## 2. Governing invariant: deploy first, improve continuously

The mandatory sequence is:

> Build → Deploy → Confirm production → Inspect → Classify → Improve → Recheck → Record

The following rules apply without exception:

- The connected three-page set deploys every day.
- Specification QA starts only after production deployment has been confirmed.
- Missing, partial, conflicting, stale, or not-yet-researched evidence does not block deployment.
- Missing polish, optional graphics, advanced motion, secondary distribution assets, or non-critical enhancements does not block deployment.
- Every known limitation must be represented honestly on the live page or in its release record.
- QA findings create fix-forward work against the live version or a later version.
- Pages and assets remain versioned, revisitable, correctable, and redistributable.
- New evidence, better explanations, improved visuals, or stronger implementation may be added after the initial release.
- No post-deployment finding may be retroactively described as a reason the original daily set should not have shipped.

## 4. QA outcomes

Tests must not use release-blocking pass/fail language. Each observation receives one of four outcomes:

| Outcome | Meaning | Required response |
|---|---|---|
| Conforming | The observed production behaviour meets the cited requirement. | Record the evidence. |
| Improvement required | The page is live but can better meet the requirement. | Create a bounded improvement and retest it after correction. |
| Unable to observe | The condition could not be assessed with the available tooling, evidence, or environment. | Record the reason and schedule another observation when useful. |
| Not applicable | The requirement does not apply to this page, asset, or release. | Record the applicability decision. |

“Unable to observe” and “improvement required” never become hidden publication gates.

## 7. Test-case contract

Every reusable test case must contain:

| Field | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Test ID | Stable identifier using `QA-{DOMAIN}-{NUMBER}`. |
| Requirement source | Exact document and section or requirement identifier. |
| Intent | The user, system, or business outcome protected by the test. |
| Applies to | Decision Hub, Solution Hub, Decision Scenario, distribution asset, or shared system. |
| Preconditions | Must include confirmed production deployment. |
| Method | Automated, manual, visual, evidence review, or mixed. |
| Viewports or agents | Required browser, device size, reduced-motion state, crawler, or consumer. |
| Procedure | Minimal repeatable observation steps. |
| Expected observation | Concrete and externally observable behaviour. |
| Actual observation | What occurred in production. |
| Evidence | URL, screenshot, trace, report, source snapshot, or measurement. |
| Outcome | Conforming, improvement required, unable to observe, or not applicable. |
| Severity | P0, P1, P2, or P3 when improvement is required. |
| Improvement action | Smallest useful correction or experiment. |
| Owner | Accountable role or worker. |
| Retest status | Not scheduled, scheduled, conforming after correction, or still improving. |

Expected observations must be measurable. Avoid vague formulations such as “looks premium,” “works well,” or “good SEO.” Translate them into observable properties.

### 8.7 Recheck and close the loop

Re-run the affected tests, attach new production evidence, update the issue state, and redistribute materially improved assets when Document 09 requires it.

### 8.8 Learn across releases

Repeated findings should improve templates, components, prompts, research operations, or deployment automation. Do not respond to every recurrence with another manual checklist item when a systemic fix is simpler.

### 9.3 Evidence, provenance, and truthfulness

| ID | Expected production observation |
|---|---|
| QA-EVID-001 | A sample of material claims can be traced to a cited source, disclosed inference, or explicit evidence-state label. |
| QA-EVID-002 | Missing evidence is stated honestly without hiding the page or replacing it with fabricated certainty. |
| QA-EVID-003 | Conflicting sources are represented as a conflict rather than silently resolved. |
| QA-EVID-004 | Time-sensitive claims expose an appropriate date or freshness signal. |
| QA-EVID-005 | Quotations, numbers, comparisons, and product claims preserve their source context. |
| QA-EVID-006 | New evidence can be attached to the existing page version history and trigger a correction or enrichment. |
| QA-EVID-007 | Affiliate or commercial relationships are not presented as independent evidence. |

### 9.4 Content and editorial quality

| ID | Expected production observation |
|---|---|
| QA-CONT-001 | The first screen communicates the decision, audience, and primary value without requiring exploratory scrolling. |
| QA-CONT-002 | Headings form a coherent outline and support scanning by humans and machines. |
| QA-CONT-003 | Claims distinguish fact, inference, recommendation, and opinion. |
| QA-CONT-004 | Definitions and decision criteria remain consistent across the three-page set. |
| QA-CONT-005 | The page provides a useful next action without forcing registration or onboarding. |
| QA-CONT-006 | Links and calls to action accurately describe their destinations. |
| QA-CONT-007 | The content contains no visible placeholders, internal prompt fragments, or unfinished production notes. |

### 9.6 Motion and interaction

| ID | Expected production observation |
|---|---|
| QA-MOT-001 | Motion explains hierarchy, causality, state, or progress rather than decorating without purpose. |
| QA-MOT-002 | Interactive elements respond consistently to pointer, keyboard, and touch input where applicable. |
| QA-MOT-003 | Reduced-motion preferences remove or simplify non-essential animation. |
| QA-MOT-004 | Motion does not delay access to principal content or obscure evidence. |
| QA-MOT-005 | Animations remain stable during loading, resizing, navigation, and repeated interaction. |
| QA-MOT-006 | Scroll-linked effects preserve reading position and do not trap or disorient the user. |

### 9.12 Commercial integrity and user trust

| ID | Expected production observation |
|---|---|
| QA-TRUST-001 | Affiliate, sponsorship, ownership, and material commercial relationships are disclosed near the relevant decision. |
| QA-TRUST-002 | Ranking, inclusion, recommendation, and exclusion criteria are understandable. |
| QA-TRUST-003 | Commercial incentives do not overwrite evidence-state labels or uncertainty. |
| QA-TRUST-004 | Corrections and material updates are visible and versioned. |
| QA-TRUST-005 | Privacy choices and telemetry disclosures match observed production behaviour. |
| QA-TRUST-006 | The public experience does not require onboarding to access the core decision value. |

## 10. Progressive QA intensity

Post-deployment QA becomes more intensive as observation capacity grows. Increased intensity must improve the product without expanding into a release veto.

## 12. Automation boundaries

Automate checks when the result is repeatable and externally observable. Good candidates include URL availability, link integrity, metadata, schema syntax, accessibility signals, performance measurements, overflow detection, console errors, sitemap inclusion, and crawler responses.

Retain human review for meaning, truthfulness, evidence context, art direction, visual hierarchy, motion purpose, recommendation integrity, and whether the page genuinely helps a decision.

Automated scores are evidence, not truth. A single aggregate score must never become a hidden release gate or replace the underlying observations.

## 16. Roles and accountability

| Role | Accountability |
|---|---|
| Deployment owner | Confirms the production page set and supplies the deployment receipt. |
| QA coordinator | Maintains traceability, chooses the applicable suite, and records outcomes without acting as a publication gatekeeper. |
| Research or evidence reviewer | Checks source relationships, claim states, freshness, and uncertainty. |
| Editorial reviewer | Checks decision usefulness, clarity, consistency, and commercial integrity. |
| Design reviewer | Checks design-system, art-direction, imagery, responsive, and motion requirements. |
| Engineering reviewer | Checks reliability, performance, accessibility implementation, metadata, telemetry, and recovery behaviour. |
| Distribution owner | Checks generated assets, canonical attribution, crawler behaviour, redistribution, and measurement. |
| Improvement owner | Applies the bounded correction and supplies retest evidence. |

One person or agent may fulfil multiple roles. Accountability must still be explicit in the record.

## 3. Why the fork is useful

The fork already contains a compact scroll runtime, declarative clip configuration, responsive conditions, reduced-motion handling, asset guidance, device diagnostics, screenshot tooling, and visual quality guidance. This is a better starting point than building another motion engine.

The fork is now a verified, vendor-neutral Codex plugin at [`bfddbd4`](https://github.com/michaelchamboko/scroll-craft/commit/bfddbd4f79d912bd20861a576527215d15c53d22), published to its `main` branch on 2026-08-30. GitHub Actions passed on that exact commit.

The published capability has a root `AGENTS.md`, a Codex marketplace catalogue, a `plugins/scroll-craft/.codex-plugin/plugin.json` manifest, canonical `skills/scrollcraft` instructions, an optional Vetted SaaS reference, Node package and lockfile, deterministic root commands, unit/browser tests, and CI. The original MIT licence and upstream attribution remain.

The hardening work also makes static semantic content visible before enhancement, exposes `mount()` teardown, cleans runtime resources, responds to operating-system reduced-motion changes, restores normal flow for reduced motion, scopes `will-change`, protects inactive worldflight content from keyboard and assistive-technology exposure, fails serious screenshot diagnostics, and binds the development server to loopback with resolved-path containment.

This is implementation-ready fork evidence, not an authority to change a Vetted SaaS production page.

### 4.1 Adjudicated engagement strategy

The product-owner direction is that motion follows **attention → understanding → confidence → action**. It may guide attention towards a qualified commercial action, including an affiliate action, only after the relevant decision has been resolved by the available evidence. Success is qualified, evidence-earned action rather than raw click pressure.

- **Decision Hubs** use the strongest evidence-led narrative progression: problem, evidence, criteria, resolution, then action.
- **Solution Hubs** use selective comparison motion only where it clarifies a meaningful criterion or outcome.
- **Decision Scenarios** use a shorter trade-off → recommendation → action sequence.

This direction is constrained by the existing evidence, ranking-independence, disclosure, and anti-deception requirements; motion cannot manufacture certainty or commercial preference.

### 5.5 Motion value test

A page may use narrative scroll motion only when all answers are yes:

1. Is there a specific uncertainty that sequence or transformation resolves?
2. Is the moving relationship easier to understand than a static arrangement?
3. Can the same content remain complete and correctly ordered without motion?
4. Can mobile and reduced-motion users reach the same conclusion without extra work?
5. Can the effect be verified with objective checkpoints?

## 7. Narrative beat model

Each scroll story should use a small number of explicit beats:

1. **Orient** - establish the decision and current state.
2. **Tension** - make the cost, trade-off, or unresolved uncertainty concrete.
3. **Explain** - reveal the model, workflow, comparison, or evidence.
4. **Resolve** - show what the evidence supports and what remains uncertain.
5. **Act** - offer the next useful step without false urgency.

Not every page needs all five beats. A sequence should contain only the beats required by the decision journey.

Each beat owns content first and motion second. The DOM must contain the complete content in the correct order before animation is attached.

## 9. Motion limits

- At most three major narrative-motion patterns per page.
- At most one dominant sticky or pinned sequence per page unless an approved exception explains the need.
- Essential content must be visible in the DOM and available without JavaScript.
- No full-page scroll hijacking or forced smooth-scroll engine.
- No animation framework may be introduced in addition to the approved production stack merely to reproduce a minor effect.
- Large parallax movement, continuous rotation, uncontrolled autoplay, and ornamental cursor effects are prohibited by default.
- Motion must stop when its section is offscreen and must clean up when the view unmounts.

### 11.2 Native platform first

Use CSS scroll-driven animations or the Web Animations API for simple, well-supported, compositor-friendly effects when the required browser matrix and fallback permit it. Use the existing ScrollCraft runtime for orchestrated multi-beat scenes, responsive scene control, and verification hooks.

This is not permission to maintain two competing motion systems. The fork must present one public narrative-motion contract and choose the smallest internal mechanism per primitive.

### 11.3 Animation properties

Prefer transforms and opacity. Layout-changing or paint-heavy animation needs an explicit performance justification and representative-device evidence. `will-change` must be temporary and narrowly applied.

### 11.4 Runtime ownership

The runtime must expose an explicit instance and diagnostic API. Verification must not depend on undocumented globals.

### 11.5 Framework adaptation

The fork provides an agent-neutral core with Codex as the canonical plugin interface. No Claude-specific manifest, marketplace, command, badge, tool declaration, or authoritative instruction file remains. Production-framework adapters remain a later, explicitly approved concern.

### Stage B: Taste direction

Taste defines composition, typography, visual rhythm, contrast, image direction, density, and the intended emotional register. Its output must identify which transitions could benefit from motion, without prescribing engine details.

### Stage C: Impeccable critique

Impeccable reviews the static and proposed-motion design for hierarchy, generic patterns, visual coherence, accessibility, responsiveness, and unnecessary complexity. It may reject motion.

## 14. Verification matrix

| Area | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Narrative | Every animated beat maps to one uncertainty and one communication job |
| Static path | Same claims, evidence, conclusion, and action are available with JavaScript disabled |
| Reduced motion | No pinned dependency, no concealed content, stable focus and anchors |
| Mobile | Separately designed sequence, no clipped or unreachable content |
| Keyboard | Logical focus order and usable controls throughout each scene |
| Screen reader | Semantic reading order is independent of visual layering |
| Performance | No sustained scroll jank; budgets pass on representative devices |
| Reliability | No console errors, failed assets, frozen scenes, or stale observers |
| Visual quality | Approved checkpoints pass Taste, Impeccable, and human review |
| Truthfulness | Motion does not imply unsupported capability or certainty |
| Analytics | Measurement distinguishes comprehension and progress from decorative engagement |
| Rollback | Feature can return to the complete static path without content loss |

## 16. Amendment map for the existing strategy set

| Document | Required amendment after approval |
|---|---|
| 01 Market Research | Add narrative comprehension as a hypothesis to validate, not an assumed competitive advantage |
| 02 Product Roadmap | Add the fork-hardening and one-page pilot as a bounded capability increment; retain the rule that nonessential motion cannot block shipping |
| 03 Architecture | Add ScrollCraft as an optional presentation capability with static fallback and explicit Global Setup boundary |
| 04 Design System | Replace broad motion guidance with the authority stack, eligibility contract, primitives, limits, and review handoff |
| 05 Master PRD | Add narrative-motion behaviour only to eligible public page requirements and preserve complete static content |
| 06 Implementation Standards | Add the fork, schema, runtime ownership, lifecycle, agent-neutral packaging, and technical acceptance contract |
| 07 Editorial Operations | Add narrative beat and motion-job fields to page briefs without making editors choose animation mechanics |
| 08 Research Operations | Add motion-pattern research as design evidence and prohibit community popularity from becoming product truth |
| 09 Growth Strategy | Define motion as a comprehension and differentiation mechanism, not a vanity acquisition tactic |
| 10 QA Plan | Add deterministic motion checkpoints, reduced-motion, mobile, performance, accessibility, rollback, and fail-closed automation |
| Approved UI Catalogue | Add motion eligibility, static fallback, performance class, provenance, and review status to component entries |

## 17. Delivery sequence after strategy approval

1. Amend Documents 04, 06, and 10 first because they establish design, implementation, and verification authority.
2. Amend Documents 05 and 07 to connect page requirements and editorial briefs.
3. Amend Documents 01, 02, 03, 08, and 09 with narrower cross-system implications.
4. Update the Approved UI Component Catalogue metadata contract.
5. Use Global Setup to produce the implementation contract, architecture map, UI contract, task graph, test plan, review gate, rollback plan, and definition of done.
6. Treat the published, verified fork as the reusable engine; do not add Vetted SaaS-specific primitives without separate production approval.
7. Build one representative pilot page with static-first markup.
8. Validate desktop, mobile, reduced motion, keyboard, screen reader, performance, and visual checkpoints.
9. Review with Taste, Impeccable, and a human decision owner.
10. Promote only proven primitives into the Narrative Interaction Vault.

The foundation phase keeps GitNexus subordinate to direct source authority.
The user directive reinforces the repository evidence and anti-invention rule.
The user directive reinforces the implementation anti-hallucination rule.
Commercial optimisation must be reconciled with ranking independence without pre-deciding the outcome.
No-commit scope limits GitNexus commit-delta analysis but not direct-source mapping.
Reduced motion remains an equivalent information-and-action experience, not a default minimal-motion preference.
ScrollCraft is primary for advanced linear narrative motion; CSS/static is baseline and GSAP is an exception, not a fallback engine.
Marketing capabilities must be selected by declared page intent and page type rather than invoked as an unrestricted bundle.
External marketing guidance remains subordinate to the local real-demand, evidence, editorial-independence, and SEO sequence.
Applicable marketing capabilities consume the existing research-context-to-page contract rather than creating a parallel product-marketing authority file.
Distribution and experimentation skills enter only after the publish, deploy, asset, telemetry, and refresh loop has reached their stage.
Marketing-generated page changes must pass the existing content, evidence, trust, distribution, and runtime QA gates.
Market-research inputs must remain observed, source-linked demand signals rather than simulated customer language or invented evidence.
Affiliate copy optimises informed progress rather than pressure or affiliate-click volume.
Pricing strategy and price anchoring are excluded while decision-relevant vendor pricing remains bound to an official source, current date, and region.
Affiliate commission, payout, vendor relationships, and campaign pressure cannot influence recommendation scoring or ranking.
Every affiliate-copy output preserves clear affiliate disclosure.
Hormozi capabilities are selected by the declared local page type rather than used as a generic sales-page bundle.
Material copy remains traceable from page-block intent through claim, evidence, source, and date.
Hormozi skills consume the existing research-context package and cannot manufacture product or market truth.
Hooks and derivative copy retain canonical identity, user context, evidence state and dates, conditions, limitations, disclosure, and a route to the full reasoning.
Every generated copy artifact remains a proposal until it passes local content and evidence QA.
Conversion design consumes the buyer-decision model.
Respect-over-manipulation refines the roadmap ethical-conversion constraint.
Ranking independence refines affiliate independence.
Editorial affiliate independence refines the architecture rule.
Motion QA verifies purposeful motion.
Motion QA verifies native scrolling.
Motion QA verifies reduced-motion equivalence.
Commercial-integrity QA verifies ranking independence.
The ScrollCraft proposal consumes design motion authority.
The ScrollCraft proposal consumes the narrative scroll-story contract.
Document 10 motion QA is the verification authority for Document 11's static, reduced-motion, keyboard, screen-reader, performance, and rollback matrix.

findings.summary: Markdown indexing alone produced containment-only edges and no semantic flows.
Some source relationship sections still describe an older ten-document set.
A stale Master PRD filename exists and is resolved only through the explicit alias registry.
The ScrollCraft fork is verified and published; D11 retains implementation_authority: false for production-page work.
The UI catalogue has no explicit D04 consumer or authority relationship.
The local foundation boundary and active-day deployment rules require later applicability adjudication.
The adjudicated motion strategy permits qualified affiliate action only after evidence resolves the relevant decision; ranking, disclosure, and anti-deception constraints remain binding.
Reduced motion must not be reinterpreted as minimal default motion.
No baseline commit means GitNexus commit-delta analysis remains unavailable.
Engineering graphs are not canonical business knowledge.
An explicit D10-to-D11 verification relationship now covers the narrative-motion verification matrix; UI-catalogue traceability remains a later amendment.
ScrollCraft is the primary advanced narrative-motion engine; CSS/static is the baseline and reduced-motion path; GSAP requires a documented branching or reversible-interaction exception.
Earlier UI catalogue drift proved the need for manifest-hash gates.

The requested marketingskills fork is pinned for review at commit 8bfcdffb655f16e713940cd04fb08891899c47db (v2.5.1, 45 skills); its skills are bounded advisory adapters and are not repository authority or an install bundle.

Generic product-marketing context, search-first prioritisation, page structures, comparison formats, and CRO defaults must yield to the existing local context, evidence order, three page-type contracts, and informed-progress conversion model.

Generic gating, social-proof, affiliate, crawler, and conversion advice must yield to public reasoning value, evidence traceability, ranking independence, disclosure, trust, consent, and crawler-policy requirements.

The fork passes its local 45-skill frontmatter and size validator, but that validator is shallow; two skills lack eval files, integration and CLI assets are not runtime-certified by the observed workflows, and the fork trails upstream.

The requested hormozi-skills fork is pinned for review at commit 25ec2b0789ae8c760b45f577024782ff399983a6; ten individual capabilities are mapped as advisory copy inputs without installing the bundle or invoking its orchestrator.

Seller-controlled pricing, guarantees, scarcity, urgency, and arbitrary bonus-value defaults conflict with an affiliate publisher that does not control the vendor offer and with local evidence and anti-deception requirements.

The reviewed fork has no observed release, CI, or eval evidence, and its full orchestrator and subagent workflow assumes Claude-specific runtime primitives; only direct individual capability calls are permitted.

Pricing strategy and monetary value anchoring are excluded from Hormozi-generated copy; decision-relevant vendor price may still be reported when verified from an official source with current date and region.
